title: Patient-specific 3D-printed four-part interlocking mold-assisted sticky bone graft shaping in late secondary alveolar bone grafting
html: Accurate graft adaptation remains a major challenge in alveolar bone grafting, especially when particulate graft materials are used. This technical note presents a digital and surgical workflow for shaping a defect-matched sticky bone graft with a patient-specific three-dimensional (3D)-printed mold. Cone-beam computed tomography-based segmentation and volumetric planning were performed in 3D Slicer, and the cleft geometry was transferred to Meshmixer for mold design. A four-part mold was fabricated to allow controlled condensation of the graft material and retrieval without fragmentation.
